items.name: The conventions file
items.blurb: Eleven rules the whole codebase actually follows. Written by someone who left. Maintained by no one. Correct anyway.
items.inspectText: Small, dense, and true. The agent reads it once and stops inventing folder structures.

items.name: The failing test output
items.blurb: One red line. It states the expected value, the actual value, and by implication the entire job.
items.inspectText: This is the requirement, wearing a stack trace. Lose it and the work becomes interpretive.

items.name: The three changed files
items.blurb: The only three files that moved in the last week. The bug is in one of them. It is always in one of them.
items.inspectText: The crime scene. Everything else in the repository is an alibi.

items.name: Docs for the API
items.blurb: Generated from the code, so it is accurate. Nobody can explain why it is accurate. Do not touch anything.

items.name: The ticket
items.blurb: The ticket describes the work. It also links to a wiki page titled 'Draft - DO NOT USE', which describes the work differently.
items.inspectText: Two sources of truth, one of them disavowed by its own title. Relevance varies by which one the author believed.

items.name: The 900-line log

scout.name: Scout report: the log
scout.blurb: Line 714: connection refused, twice, at the exact timestamp of the failure. The other 899 lines were the system agreeing with itself.

items.blurb: Nine hundred lines. One of them is the error. It is not near the top, it is not near the bottom, and it is not marked ERROR.
items.inspectText: One line in here matters. Carrying all 900 to find it is a choice. Sending someone with their own bag is another.

items.name: 6 months of scrollback

scout.name: Scout report: the scrollback
scout.blurb: In March, at 11:48 PM, someone renamed the status field and everyone reacted with a thumbs up. That was the documentation.

items.blurb: Somewhere in here, one decision was made. It was never written down anywhere else. The rest is lunch plans and a recurring argument about time zones.
items.inspectText: Contains exactly one load-bearing sentence. The archaeology is the expensive part.

items.name: Full directory listing

scout.name: Scout report: the tree
scout.blurb: There are four files that matter. You are already carrying three of them. The fourth is the conventions file. You have that too.

items.blurb: Every file in the repository, alphabetically. Comforting the way a phone book is comforting.
items.inspectText: Knowing where everything is, is not the same as needing everything.

items.name: node_modules

scout.name: Scout report: node_modules
scout.blurb: The scout returned after three days. The report reads, in full: 'It's dependencies all the way down. Do not follow me in here.'

items.blurb: Fourteen thousand folders. The agent needs none of them. Given the chance, it will read all of them.
items.inspectText: Heavier than the wagon. Heavier than the canyon. Some things are not cargo.

items.name: README.md (3 years old)
items.blurb: Describes, with great warmth, a framework the project migrated off in 2023. The setup instructions end at step 4 of 9.
items.inspectText: Historical fiction. The agent will believe every word.

items.name: Architecture diagram
items.blurb: Boxes and arrows. Two of the boxes were never built. The arrows describe how data was supposed to feel.
items.inspectText: Aspirational. The system in this diagram would not have your bug. The system you have does.

items.name: The style thread (400)

scout.name: Scout report: the thread
scout.blurb: Tabs won. Then spaces won. Then a linter was installed and everyone lost together. Recommendation: use the linter.

items.blurb: Tabs versus spaces, escalated to a director. Resolved by a linter that everyone resents equally, which is what resolution means here.
items.inspectText: Four hundred comments, zero requirements. Pure sediment.

items.name: Stack trace, wrong bug
items.blurb: It is beautiful. It is complete. It has line numbers and everything. It belongs to somebody else's problem.
items.inspectText: The right shape, the wrong crime. Pack it and the agent will heroically fix a thing that is not broken.

items.name: The passing test output
items.blurb: Four hundred green checkmarks. The agent finds them soothing. So do you. That is the problem.
items.inspectText: Reassurance weighs six slots and answers no questions.

strings.intro: The canyon is exactly as wide as your wagon. Your wagon is exactly as wide as what you choose to carry. Choose.
strings.peekNotice: You take a look. Reading costs a token. It always has; you just never itemized it.
strings.overflow: THE WALLS MOVE. The canyon does not negotiate with cargo. The last item is back on the ground and the wagon is worse for it.
strings.overflowNodeModules: The wagon does not creak. Creaking implies survivors. node_modules stays on the ground, where it has always technically worked.
strings.compactNotice: Compacted. The summary reads clean. Summaries always read clean.
strings.compactRequirementLost: The summary of the summary is excellent. Somewhere between drafts, one sentence stopped being mentioned. Nothing flags this. Nothing ever does.
strings.scoutDepart: The scout shoulders a small bag of their own and walks into the noise.
strings.scoutFirst: They read the whole thing so the wagon doesn't have to. One slot. This is the trick. This has always been the trick.
strings.markNotice: Left behind, location noted. The agent can go back for it mid-loop. Going back is never free, it is only later.
strings.unmarkNotice: Unmarked. If the agent needs it now, it will have to already have it.
strings.departRetrieval: Mid-loop, the agent goes back for what you marked. Each trip costs a tool call. The canyon watches it jog.
strings.wrongProblem: The pack was light. The agent, unburdened by your actual situation, solves a problem you don't have. Beautifully. In four files. There are tests.
strings.requirementLostOutcome: The pack was tight. The work was clean. The requirement was in the part of the summary that didn't survive the second pass. What shipped is a very good answer to a question nobody asked.
strings.successPass: The wagon clears the walls with a hand's width to spare. Everything aboard earns its slot. Nothing aboard is company.
strings.successTight: The wagon glides through. A party at the entrance, still loading their directory listing, watches you go. One of them takes a note. The note is too long.
strings.retryPrompt: The four beautiful wrong files are reverted. The canyon is still here. So is the pile.
strings.requirementRestored: You re-run the failing test. The requirement states itself again, verbatim, unbothered. Durable sources do that.
